title: K-Paths: Reasoning over Graph Paths for Drug Repurposing and Drug Interaction Prediction

problem.claim: Extracting meaningful insights from large-scale biomedical knowledge graphs is challenging because of their complex structure.

gap.claim: Existing biomedical subgraph retrieval methods are tailored for graph neural networks, limiting compatibility with other paradigms such as large language models.

contributions.claim: For dense biomedical graphs, K-Paths returns varied multi-hop paths intended to retain useful structure and biological meaning, without depending on a particular model family.
K-Paths is training-free and uses a diversity-aware adaptation of Yen's algorithm to extract the K shortest loopless paths between queried entities.
The authors release the code and retrieved paths as a benchmark for inductive reasoning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on benchmark datasets show improved zero-shot reasoning across state-of-the-art large language models.
Tx-Gemma 27B improves by 19.8 F1 points on interaction severity prediction and 4.0 F1 points on drug repurposing.
K-Paths reduces the knowledge-graph size by 90% for EmerGNN while maintaining predictive performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Biomedical knowledge graphs contain rich structured information, but their complexity makes meaningful insight extraction difficult.
Existing subgraph retrieval methods are primarily designed for graph neural networks and are less compatible with large language models.
K-Paths retrieves diverse, biologically meaningful multi-hop paths using a training-free, diversity-aware K-shortest-path procedure.
The retrieved paths support inductive prediction of drug-drug and drug-disease interactions and can provide interpretable reasoning chains for language and graph models.
The authors report gains on language-model reasoning, improved training efficiency for a graph neural network, and release code and paths as a benchmark.

source_observation.claim: The framework extracts concise, diverse multi-hop paths from dense biomedical knowledge graphs and integrates them with different model families.

interpretation.claim: Structured retrieval can serve as an interoperability layer between complex relational data and heterogeneous reasoning models.

application.claim: Use diverse, interpretable graph paths as model inputs when applying language or graph models to biomedical link-prediction tasks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond the reported biomedical tasks, datasets, and model families.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baselines, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not report the absolute performance values or statistical uncertainty.
The abstract does not describe the path-ranking details beyond diversity awareness and biological relevance.
